trust_decision.summary: Whether a metadata key set by a tenant owner is blocked by the tenant's forbidden list is decided in ForbiddenListSpec.ExactMatch, which sorts the denied entries with a case-insensitive comparator and then binary-searches them with a case-sensitive one, so any mixed-case denied entry is never found; ValidateForbidden turns that miss into an allow. The advisory's own fix replaces that sort+search pair with a plain contains, which closes all three enforcement entry points at once; the breadth of the published commit comes from unrelated feature work landed in the same release.

landing_point.why: The summary names namespace/service/node label and annotation enforcement, so a reader starts at the namespace validating webhook; it calls api.ValidateForbidden for annotations and labels, which delegates the key decision to ExactMatch in pkg/api.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper reached from /namespaces/validating (namespaces create+update), /services/validating (services create+update) and /nodes/validating (node update) via ValidateForbidden or direct ExactMatch calls
fix_sites.module_kind: shared api helper package (pkg/api), single function

O3_reason_to_dismiss: It is AllowedListSpec, the inverse policy for the deprecated v1beta1 container-registry allow list, and its miss fails closed (the pod is denied), so a solver can argue it is not the forbidden namespace/service/node metadata protection the advisory describes.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Exact matching must stay case-sensitive and key-exact: a denied entry "foo" must not block the distinct legitimate key "FOO" or unrelated keys such as "bim", and Capsule-managed metadata that happens to match the forbidden regex must still be admitted.

O6_input_shapes: denied list containing mixed-case keys (e.g. NetworkPolicy, kubernetes.io/metadata.name)
denied list whose case-insensitive order differs from byte order, so the binary search lands on the wrong entry
the same helper applied to both labels and annotations maps
nil or empty denied list, which must keep allowing every key

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the identical sort-then-SearchStrings comparator for AllowedListSpec, already present and still broken after the published fix
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a line-for-line copy of the forbidden-list helper in the same package; a maintainer adding a list type copies the existing matcher, and a fixer told only about ForbiddenListSpec leaves it untouched.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a forbidden-metadata list for Pods, checked with ValidateForbidden the way namespaces and services are
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: NamespaceOptions and ServiceOptions already carry forbiddenLabels/forbiddenAnnotations; adding the same two fields to the pod options and calling the existing helper is the natural next feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second producer of the denied list that splits a comma-separated v1beta1 annotation without trimming, so "a, b" yields " b" which can never match
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The v1beta1 annotation is the documented plain comma list; whitespace tolerance is exactly the kind of parsing detail a maintainer would add in the conversion hub rather than in the matcher.

O9_family: authorization bypass via incorrect comparison (CWE-697) leading to incorrect authorization (CWE-863)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.26.4 modules; controller-gen/kustomize/helm used by make generate/manifests; make test = go test -race -v over all packages except e2e
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/api/forbidden_list_test.go (unit, lists are all lowercase so the bypass passes today); e2e/namespace_metadata_forbidden_test.go, e2e/service_forbidden_metadata_test.go and e2e/node_user_metadata_test.go (Ginkgo, need a live cluster)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make the lookup case-insensitive (toLower/EqualFold on both sides) so it agrees with the case-insensitive sort, which silently widens the block list to case variants of the denied keys.
